comment: Estimates in seconds, used only to balance the shards, to order them (longest first) and to derive the job timeouts. A wrong value unbalances the shards and breaks nothing. Measured on GitHub runners (ubuntu-24.04, 4 vCPU) in the runs of 2026-11-19 to 2026-11-21, as the 'ok' seconds of go test in the shard logs: internal/lint 243, internal/adminapi 422, internal/store 138, internal/app 85, internal/worker/smssend 61, internal/admincli 45, internal/auth/session 34, internal/auth/login 26, and the oracle shards of internal/api 90 to 134 each (api_split is their mean), internal/api without them 555 to 620. internal/store/catalogtest 119 (run 44732890797, shard packages-2). MUTANTS (round 16, run 44855288724 of 2026-11-21, six shards of 134 to 207 mutants, two at a time): the shard logs print one 'killed' line per mutant with its time, and the gap before a line is what the mutant cost in wall time. Over the 881 mutants whose gap was under 10 seconds the mean gap was 2.62 seconds per must_fail run of a plain mutant and 3.77 of a container one, so mutant.plain_run is 3 and mutant.docker_run is 4 (before: 4 and 12, a guess that put the container mutants three times above the plain ones when they are one and a half times). The 87 mutants whose gap was 10 seconds or more (a Valkey or Postgres start-up that the test waits for, a baseline run of a package) are listed by id in mutant_seconds with that gap, and an entry from the round 13 measurement stays when it is larger; the table replaces the per-run cost of that mutant. With these numbers the six shards of that run would have cost 667 to 915 seconds each (the sum of the gaps of their mutants), where the old estimate gave 438 to 1441 for the same estimate. The next green run (44870914558) did NOT confirm that balance (CI review round 17, ci-r17-3): the shards took 599 to 1350 seconds, a ratio of 2.25, and only 34 of the 87 listed mutants had a gap of 10 seconds or more again. A gap is where the wait for a start-up lands (a Valkey or Postgres container that the first mutant of a worker that needs it waits for, a baseline run), so it follows the order the mutants ran in and is not a cost of the mutant; only the mutants that were slow in both runs (the Valkey sweep mutants: 281 and 348, 220 and 265 seconds) are slow by themselves. So the estimate balances the shards on a best guess, it promises no ratio between the longest and the shortest, and it does not track the wall time; nothing depends on that, because the job bounds come from wall_percent below. The baseline numbers (plain_baseline and docker_baseline) are not measured and stay at the defaults. TIMEOUTS (ci-r16-1): the job bound of a shard is timeout_factor times its measured wall time, with a floor of timeout_floor_minutes. wall_percent is the longest wall time measured for a kind of shard (job start to end, setup included) as a percent of the estimate of that shard: packages 469 s of 811 (58), api-rest 614 s of 560 (110), api-split 220 s of 112 (196), mutants 1495 s of 4417 (34, the slowest shard of the run over the heaviest shard of the new plan, so it is not too small once the shards are balanced). Refresh them from the shard table of a green run when the Panel grows; a bound that is too small fails a green run, so keep the factor at 3 or more.
